attribution: Extract, colour, and diastatic-power figures transcribed from maltster technical data sheets (Weyermann, Briess, Crisp, Simpsons, Castle, Best Malz, Rahr, Great Western, Muntons, Thomas Fawcett) and standard brewing references. Ranges vary by crop year and maltster — always confirm on the bag.

fermentables.name: 2-Row Pale Malt
fermentables.description: The default American base malt. Clean, mildly sweet, plenty of diastatic power to convert itself and a load of adjuncts.

fermentables.name: 6-Row Pale Malt
fermentables.description: Higher protein and higher diastatic power than 2-row, lower extract. The classic choice when a grist carries a lot of corn or rice.
fermentables.usageNotes: Its enzyme surplus is why American adjunct lagers use it.

fermentables.name: Maris Otter
fermentables.description: The benchmark English floor-malted base; rich, biscuity, bready depth that plain pale malt lacks.

fermentables.name: Golden Promise
fermentables.description: Scottish base malt, softer and cleaner than Maris Otter. A staple of Scotch whisky distilling as well as brewing.

fermentables.name: Pilsner Malt
fermentables.description: Continental lager base malt, kilned very lightly for a pale, delicate, honeyed malt character.
fermentables.usageNotes: High in SMM/DMS precursors — give it a vigorous 90-minute boil.

fermentables.name: Vienna Malt
fermentables.description: Lightly toasted base malt bridging Pilsner and Munich; golden colour with a soft toasty sweetness.

fermentables.name: Munich Malt (Light)
fermentables.description: Malt-forward base with enough enzyme to convert itself; the backbone of Märzen, bock, and dunkel.

fermentables.name: Munich Malt (Dark)
fermentables.description: Darker, richer Munich; intense malty depth with marginal enzyme reserve.

fermentables.name: Pale Ale Malt
fermentables.description: Slightly darker, fuller-bodied kilned base malt for ales.

fermentables.name: Pale Wheat Malt
fermentables.description: Malted wheat: boosts body, head retention, and haze. The base of German weissbier at 50–70% of the grist.
fermentables.usageNotes: Huskless — pair with rice hulls or barley malt to avoid a stuck sparge.

fermentables.name: Dark Wheat Malt
fermentables.description: Kilned darker for dunkelweizen depth while keeping wheat's protein and head retention.

fermentables.name: Rye Malt
fermentables.description: Malted rye — dry, peppery, spicy, with a silky mouthfeel. Also a whiskey mash staple.
fermentables.usageNotes: Very gummy (beta-glucans); rice hulls strongly recommended above ~20%.

fermentables.name: Acidulated Malt
fermentables.description: Malt coated in lactic acid from a natural souring step; used to drop mash pH without mineral additions. Roughly 1% of the grist lowers pH by ~0.1.

fermentables.name: Carapils / Dextrine Malt
fermentables.description: Adds unfermentable dextrins for body and head retention with essentially no colour or flavour.

fermentables.name: Crystal Malt 20L
fermentables.description: Light caramel malt; mild sweetness and golden colour without heaviness.

fermentables.name: Crystal Malt 40L
fermentables.description: The workhorse caramel malt — toffee sweetness and amber colour in pale ales and ambers.

fermentables.name: Crystal Malt 60L
fermentables.description: Deeper caramel with a hint of raisin; standard in ambers, bitters, and porters.

fermentables.name: Crystal Malt 120L
fermentables.description: Dark crystal — raisin, burnt sugar, and dried fruit. Heavy-handed above ~5% of the grist.

fermentables.name: Special B
fermentables.description: The most intense Belgian caramel malt; unmistakable dark raisin and plum. A signature of dubbels.

fermentables.name: Melanoidin Malt
fermentables.description: Intensifies malt aroma and red hues, mimicking the effect of decoction mashing.

fermentables.name: Biscuit Malt
fermentables.description: Lightly roasted for warm bread-crust and biscuit character.

fermentables.name: Victory Malt
fermentables.description: Toasted malt with a nutty, biscuity bite.

fermentables.name: Aromatic Malt
fermentables.description: Very malt-aromatic, boosts malt intensity in Belgian and malty styles.

fermentables.name: Honey Malt
fermentables.description: Intensely sweet, honeyed malt with no actual honey; a little goes a long way.

fermentables.name: Chocolate Malt
fermentables.description: Roasted to a smooth cocoa and coffee character; the colour backbone of porters.

fermentables.name: Black Patent Malt
fermentables.description: Maximum colour with a sharp, acrid roast. Use sparingly for colour correction or dry-stout bite.

fermentables.name: Roasted Barley
fermentables.description: Unmalted barley roasted dark — the defining sharp, coffee-like dryness of Irish dry stout.

fermentables.name: Carafa Special Type II
fermentables.description: Dehusked roasted malt: deep colour and cocoa without the astringent bite of husked roast malts.
fermentables.usageNotes: The standard way to darken a beer smoothly — ideal for schwarzbier and black IPA.

fermentables.name: Beechwood Smoked Malt
fermentables.description: Kilned over beechwood for the classic Bamberg rauchbier smoke. Can be used as the whole base malt.

fermentables.name: Peated Malt
fermentables.description: Peat-smoked malt — medicinal, earthy smoke. The signature of Islay whisky; use tiny amounts in beer.

fermentables.name: Brown Malt
fermentables.description: Dry, toasty, coffee-ish English malt central to historical porters.

fermentables.name: Amber Malt
fermentables.description: Toasted English malt with a dry biscuit character for milds, browns, and porters.

fermentables.name: Chit Malt
fermentables.description: Barely-germinated malt high in protein; improves foam and body, popular in hazy IPAs.

fermentables.name: CaraMunich III
fermentables.description: German caramel malt with intense malty-sweet, light-raisin depth; the continental counterpart to English crystal.

fermentables.name: CaraHell
fermentables.description: Light German caramel malt for body and gentle sweetness in Helles, bock, and pale lagers.

fermentables.name: CaraRed
fermentables.description: Adds a warm red-amber hue and light caramel to red ales and amber lagers.

fermentables.name: Carafa Special Type I
fermentables.description: The lightest dehusked Carafa; smooth colour and mild cocoa without husk astringency.

fermentables.name: Golden Naked Oats
fermentables.description: Huskless malted oat crystal malt; nutty, creamy, silky mouthfeel. A hazy-IPA and oatmeal favourite.

fermentables.name: Oat Malt
fermentables.description: Malted (rather than flaked) oats — silky body with more enzyme than raw oats, easier to mash.

fermentables.name: Abbey Malt
fermentables.description: Malty, bready specialty malt with a hint of dark fruit for Belgian and strong ales.

fermentables.name: Cherrywood Smoked Malt
fermentables.description: American malt smoked over cherrywood for a sweeter, fruitier smoke than beechwood.

fermentables.name: Pale Chocolate Malt
fermentables.description: Lighter than full chocolate malt; deep colour with a softer, less acrid cocoa character.
